# Avera Cancer Institute holds grand opening for new facility in Yankton

Dakota News Now Youtube Promo

By Dakota News Now staff

Published: Jun. 30, 2026 at 9:32 AM CDT


YANKTON, S.D. (Dakota News Now) - The Avera Cancer Institute’s Ness Family Center held a grand opening on June 26.

The $17 million facility is located in the Ness Family Center, named in honor of Larry and Diane Ness, who made a significant lead gift and offered a $500,000 match for community donations through First Dakota National Bank.

The grand opening featured speakers, a ribbon-cutting ceremony with Yankton Thrive, and tours.

“Today is about much more than opening a new building. It’s about creating a beautiful, healing space that will make a positive impact for patients and families across Yankton and the surrounding region,” said Vice President for Oncology at Avera, Katie VanBeek.

“Here, patients can access a whole host of first-class cancer resources under one roof. That means more time focused on what matters most – healing, hope and spending time with loved ones. This building is more than bricks and mortar. It is a reflection of our mission, our people, and our commitment to ensuring that patients in this community can receive high-quality cancer care close to home.”

Image: Avera Cancer Institute holds grand opening for new facility in Yankton

Avera Cancer Institute holds grand opening for new facility in Yankton(Avera Health)

The Avera Cancer Institute consists of six regional centers and numerous outreach and telemedicine sites, forming the region’s only accredited cancer care network by the American College of Surgeons and the American Society of Clinical Oncology.

“The new Avera Cancer Institute location offers medical oncology, radiation oncology, chemotherapy infusion, clinical research, genetic counseling and other support services in one location instead of across two locations in Yankton,” said Regional President and CEO of Avera Sacred Heart Hospital, Victoria Hanson.

“Having all services in one place aligns the Yankton center with Avera’s oncology locations in Aberdeen, Mitchell, Pierre and Sioux Falls, SD, and Marshall, MN, ensuring that patients receive the same, consistent experience.”

Previously, radiation oncology was at the Avera Cancer Institute, while medical oncology and infusions were at Avera Sacred Heart Hospital.

“This is a very special place, and one reason is that hope lives within these walls,” Hanson said.

“Supporters of the project wrote messages of support to the patients and their loved ones who will seek care here within the walls around the building as it was being constructed. Today, I invite you to feel the strength of those prayers and intentions as you walk through this beautiful facility.”

A portion of the funding for the project came from the Avera Foundation’s $7 million “Building Hope Here” campaign, which is continuing to accept donations.

You can learn more about the Building Hope campaign at averafoundation.org/buildinghopehere.

# Landmark gift establishes Sanford Black Hills Medical Center

## $300 million investment will bring world-class specialty care to Black Hills region

Written by Paul Heinert

November 17, 2025

7 min read


Image: Landmark gift establishes Sanford Black Hills Medical Center

The new Sanford Black Hills Medical Center campus in Rapid City, South Dakota, will expand access to specialty care and services including an emergency department, ICU, oncology center, comprehensive women’s health including a labor and delivery unit, and children’s services. (Rendering by Sanford Health)

Sanford Health announced today another landmark gift from the world’s greatest health care philanthropist that will transform health care in western South Dakota and the Black Hills region for generations to come.

Denny Sanford has made a $300 million philanthropic gift to Sanford Health to help establish the Sanford Black Hills Medical Center campus in Rapid City, South Dakota.

The new state-of-the-art medical center campus will expand access to specialty care and services including an emergency department, ICU, oncology center, comprehensive women’s health including a labor and delivery unit, and children’s services.

“Mr. Sanford’s extraordinary generosity and vision inspire what we do every day at Sanford Health. His philanthropic gifts have transformed health care across the region, touched the lives of millions and will continue to benefit the communities we serve for generations to come,” said Bill Gassen, president and CEO of Sanford Health. “We are honored to carry forward his remarkable legacy in the Black Hills.”

## Plans for Rapid City campus

The campus will be located in southwest Rapid City, adjacent to the Black Hills Orthopedic and Spine Center. Construction is scheduled to begin in 2027 with completion expected by 2030.

The proposed 480,000-square-feet Sanford Black Hills Medical Center campus will include:

  * 168 inpatient beds
  * Future campus expansion for additional 168 beds
  * Emergency department bays
  * Surgical suites and procedure rooms
  * Cath labs
  * Full inpatient and outpatient imaging suites
  * Dialysis center
  * Oncology infusion center
  * Children’s outpatient and inpatient services

# Landmark gift establishes Sanford Black Hills Medical Center

November 21, 2025

Image: Sanford-Health-02-1_SHN-webAn architect's rendering of the future Sanford Black Hills Medical Center

The South Dakota Association of Healthcare Organizations (SDAHO) is pleased to share news of a significant health care expansion in Rapid City. Earlier this week, Sanford Health announced plans for the new Sanford Black Hills Medical Center Campus, which will expand access to specialty care and essential services, including an emergency department, ICU, oncology center, comprehensive women’s health with a labor and delivery unit, and children’s services.

The Announcement released November 17, 2025 – https://news.sanfordhealth.org/news/landmark-gift-establishes-sanford-black-hills-medical-center/

Sanford Health announced another landmark gift from the world’s greatest health care philanthropist that will transform health care in western South Dakota and the Black Hills region for generations to come.

Denny Sanford has made a $300 million philanthropic gift to Sanford Health to help establish the Sanford Black Hills Medical Center campus in Rapid City, South Dakota.

The new state-of-the-art medical center campus will expand access to specialty care and services including an emergency department, ICU, oncology center, comprehensive women’s health including a labor and delivery unit, and children’s services.

Since 2004, Mr. Sanford has given nearly $2 billion to Sanford Health. What began with his first gift to establish the Sanford Children’s Hospital in 2004 has grown into a legacy of transformative philanthropy.

In 2021, he made a historic $650 million investment, launching a groundbreaking virtual care initiative that is redefining how patients access care by connecting world-class clinicians and technology to communities across the upper Midwest and expanding graduate medical education programs to strengthen the rural physician pipeline.
Construction is scheduled to begin in 2027 with completion expected by 2030.

The proposed 480,000-square-feet Sanford Black Hills Medical Center campus will include:

  * 168 inpatient beds
  * Future campus expansion for additional 168 beds
  * Emergency department bays
  * Surgical suites and procedure rooms
  * Cath labs
  * Full inpatient and outpatient imaging suites
  * Dialysis center
  * Oncology infusion center
  * Children’s outpatient and inpatient services

Investing in medical education

Starting in 2026, Sanford Health intends to invest $10 million over the next decade to partner with K-12 schools, technical colleges and universities across the Black Hills including:

  * $2.5 million: Expand the Aspire program to foster students’ interest in health care and provide hands-on learning opportunities for more than 13,000 K-12 students
  * $3 million: Invest in Build Dakota to support in-demand technical education
  * $4.5 million: Expand sponsorships at regional post-secondary educational institutions

Lauren Soulek

SIOUX FALLS, S.D. (KELO) – A new veterinary hospital has opened in Sioux Falls and its operating as a non-profit with a mission to make care more accessible.

Inside PetSmart you’ll now find one of two Pet Wellness Veterinary Hospitals of the Hanson Family Foundation.

“We’re really excited and proud to say that we are South Dakota’s first non-profit hospital, so we’re a hospital with a mission,” Heidi Dean, the director of community relations and marketing, said.

And that mission is two-fold.

“One, we’re here to make access to quality veterinarian medicine more affordable to people in the Sioux Falls area,” Dr. Al Harrist said. “And then the second is the opportunity for the community to pay it forward.
